item_coverage.title: A modulus need not be a conductor
The Euler-product identity does not survive after leaving the absolute half-plane
A generalized Pell solution need not be a convergent
Ramified frobenius has no canonical lift
$7$ and $28$ are not sums of three integer squares
The average order of Euler's totient is 6n over pi squared
Convergents are reduced fractions
An Eisenstein prime is totally ramified
Frobenius compatibility in finite towers
The Dirichlet series of the Möbius function is the reciprocal of the zeta Dirichlet series on Re s greater than 1
The number of square roots of a unit modulo $n$ is the product of the local counts
Every prime modulus admits a primitive root
Sums of two squares are closed under products
Möbius inversion gives $\Lambda=\mu*\log$
Associates in $\mathbb{Z}$: integers each of which divides the other
Cyclotomic conductor of a full cyclotomic field
Dirichlet L-functions
The p-adic numbers as a metric completion
Inertia group of a prime
Logarithmic embedding of a number field
Regulator of a number field
Primes above and residue degree
Quadratic residues and nonresidues modulo an integer
Successive minima of a convex body
$7$ and $28$ have four-square representations with no zero coordinate
The Chinese remainder bijection $\mathbb{Z}/12\to\mathbb{Z}/3\times\mathbb{Z}/4$ computed on all standard representatives
Decomposition groups in a tower
Boundary behavior can agree or differ for Dirichlet-series abscissae
A local prime factor in the Dirichlet series of Euler's totient
Four essentially different four-square representations of $65$
$\gcd$ at the boundary: $\gcd(a,0) = |a|$, $\gcd(0,0) = 0$, and the convention $\gcd(0,0) = 0$ is exactly what makes $\gcd(ca,cb) = |c|\gcd(a,b)$ true at $c = 0$
Computing $(1111/8093)$ by the Euclidean Jacobi algorithm
The first coefficients of 1 over zeta are the Möbius values
The p-adic expansion of minus one
Prime decomposition in Q(zeta_8)
The primitive two-square criterion distinguishes $289$, $34$, and $833$
Real quadratic units and Pell's equation
S-units of Q
The character chi_4 and the Gregory-Leibniz series
$2$ is prime, and it is the only even prime: every even integer $n > 2$ is composite
The von Mangoldt residue table
A number-field unit is exactly an algebraic integer of norm plus or minus one
Prime valuations in the central binomial coefficient
Convergent error bound
Character values on units are roots of unity
Finitely many ideals of bounded norm
$\gcd$ is symmetric and unchanged by signs: $\gcd(a,b) = \gcd(b,a) = \gcd(|a|,|b|)$; moreover $\gcd(a,0) = |a|$, $\gcd(a,1) = 1$, $\gcd(a,a) = |a|$, and $\gcd(a,b) \ge 1$ unless $a = b = 0$
A nonempty set of integers bounded above has a greatest element, and a nonempty set of integers bounded below has a least element
A left-half-plane bound for the logarithmic derivative of zeta
Nonprincipal Dirichlet character partial sums are bounded
$v_p(ab) = v_p(a) + v_p(b)$ for nonzero integers $a, b$, and $v_p(a+b) \ge \min\{v_p(a), v_p(b)\}$ whenever $a$, $b$ and $a+b$ are all nonzero
Powers of primes congruent to $1$ modulo $4$ have primitive two-square representations
Finitely many roots of unity in a number field
Thue's lemma on small nonzero representatives
In $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times$, inversion pairs every class except $[1]_p$ and $[-1]_p$, which are the only self-inverse classes
Every nonzero residue modulo an odd prime is a sum of two squares
A unit is a primitive root modulo $n$ if and only if it generates $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^\times$

Bézout's identity: for integers $a, b$ not both zero, $\gcd(a,b)$ is the least positive element of $\{\, ax + by : x, y \in \mathbb{Z} \,\}$; in particular $ax + by = \gcd(a,b)$ has an integer solution
Conductor of a full cyclotomic field
Decomposition and inertia in towers
An arithmetic function has a Dirichlet inverse exactly when its value at $1$ is nonzero
Multiplying absolutely convergent Dirichlet series gives Dirichlet convolution
The Euclidean algorithm: for $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $b > 0$ the remainder descent from $(a,b)$ terminates, and the last nonzero remainder is $\gcd(a,b)$
Finiteness of the number-field class group

For positive integers $a$ and $b$ and every prime $p$: $v_p(\gcd(a,b)) = \min\{v_p(a), v_p(b)\}$ and $v_p(\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)) = \max\{v_p(a), v_p(b)\}$; so the exponent-wise greatest common divisor is the $\gcd$ of the divisibility page and not a second notion
Finite Euler factors under character induction
Landau's theorem for Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients
A multiplicative Dirichlet series factors as an Euler product on its absolute half-plane
The regulator is well defined
Power-basis and polynomial discriminants
Characterisation of primitive sums of two squares
The nonzero squares modulo an odd prime form an index-two subgroup
The ring of integers has rank the degree
The unit group modulo $n$ is the product of its odd-prime cyclic factors and its explicit $2$-power factor
Each proper-equivalence class of positive-definite integral binary quadratic forms contains exactly one reduced form
Unramified frobenius element exists uniquely
